text: Hello and welcome to coverage of the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and Burnley at Kenilworth Road.
Burnley travel to Kenilworth Road to face Luton Town in the Premier League in a game which sees two newly promoted sides go head-to-head.

Rob Edwards and Vincent Kompany have struggled to get a tune out of their respective sides in England’s top flight so far this season, with Burnley sitting in 19th place and Luton just outside the relegation zone in 16th.
Luton will be looking to build on an excellent victory away to Everton at Goodison Park on Saturday in what was their first three points of the Premier League season.
Burnley are yet to pick up their first win of the campaign, drawing once and losing five of their opening six fixtures.
A win for the Clarets could see Kompany’s men climb out of the relegation zone, whereas the Hatters will be four points above the drop zone if they are victorious.
Kompany has made just one change from his Burnley side who lost 2-0 against Newcastle United at St James’ Park on the weekend.
Ramsey drops to the bench with Foster returning to the starting XI.

Edwards has also only made one adjustment to his Luton XI after their 2-1 win over Everton at Goodison Park, with Burke being replaced by Mengi, who makes his first Premier League start of the season in defence.
After a tricky start to their first-ever season in the Premier League, Luton are now unbeaten in two games and will be hoping to extend that against a struggling Burnley.
Kompany will welcome the return of Foster, who is the Clarets' leading goalscorer in the league this term with two strikes.
The players are on the pitch ready for kick-off.
The game is under way!
Burnley have started the game with a little more attacking intent, as Kompany's side look to dominate possession and break Luton down.
Chance for Luton! Morris finds space in the box after a clever pass from Kabore, and the Hatters striker fires across the penalty area but can't quite find Ogbene at the back post.
Taylor breaks down the left for Burnley and bursts into the box.
He finds Amdouni in the penalty area but the Luton defence deal with the danger and clear for a corner.
Luton look to create a dangerous opportunity with a long throw into the Burnley box, but the ball eventually lands in the hands of Trafford.
Burnley get a free-kick deep inside the Luton half which whips into the box, but the assistant referee flags for offside.
Burnley are enjoying more of the ball so far with 70 per cent possession, but are struggling to break Luton down in the opening stages of the game.
Mpanzu picks up a loose ball just outside the Burnley box and unleashes a strike from range, but the effort goes comfortably wide of Trafford's goal.
Foster does superbly to drive through the Luton defence, riding multiple challenges before looking to strike one towards goal from outside the box, but the ball flies past the post.
Burnley look to break down the right-hand side with Koleosho, but Nakamba does superbly to intervene and clear the ball out for a corner.
Bell is struggling with an injury and the medical team enter the pitch.
Bell can't continue after his injury and is replaced by Burke.
CHANCE! Burnley have an excellent opportunity to convert from a corner, but Kaminski makes an excellent save to deny Amdouni's bullet header.
The Hatters forward will feel he should have put his side ahead.
Amdouni shows his trickery on the left-hand side to break into the Luton box, but the defence are equal to it and cut out the danger.
Close! Brownhill finds himself in space outside the box and looks to curl one beyond Kaminski in the Luton goal, but the goal goes narrowly over the bar.
Another half-chance for Burnley goes begging.
Amdouni pokes the ball past a Luton defender and looks to unleash a strike from range, but the shot flies over the bar and out for a goal-kick.
CHANCE! Ogbene has an excellent opportunity to put Luton in the lead.
Kabore delivers a fantastic cross into the box but Ogbene can only divert his header over the bar.
Luton are starting to show a little more threat in the final third as Brown can't quite guide his header on target after another delivery into the penalty area.
Brown goes into the book after a late challenge on Cullen in the Burnley half.
Koleosho is the next Burnley player to try and test the Luton goal after weaving through the defence, but he can only send his strike into the stands.
Doughty clashes with Roberts off the pitch and the Luton faithful aren't happy.
The referee has a word with both players and the game resumes.
Koleosho dances through the Luton defence on the right-hand side and delivers a ball towards the back post, but Kabore does enough to guide it out for a corner to Burnley.
Burnley work the ball well towards the Luton goal.
It eventually drops to Brownhill just outside the box but he drags his shot wide of the post.
There will be three minutes of added time in the first half.
GOAAAAAAAAL!!! 1-0 Burnley!!! Foster latches on to a superb throughball from Berge beyond the Luton defence and places the ball under Kaminski and into the back of the net.
The Hatters striker grabs his third goal of the season to give his side the lead at Kenilworth Road.
Berge timed his pass to perfection allowing Foster to beat the offside trap and race past the Luton defenders to slot the ball home.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-1 BURNLEY
Neither side had too many clear-cut chances in the first half, but Kompany will of course be the happier of the two managers after Burnley opened scoring late on.
Luton sat deep absorbing the pressure whilst looking to counter-attack, but the Clarets found a breakthrough through Foster.
Edwards won't be too disheartened with his side's performance, but he won't be happy with the goal conceded as the Hatters' defence was left exposed on the break.
Luton will still feel they have a chance of picking up points in this game after limiting Burnley's chances to score in the first 45 minutes.
The Hatters had some opportunities of their own, but are yet to properly test Trafford's goal.
Kompany will be desperate for the Clarets to hold on as they are just one half of football away from their first victory back in the Premier League.
The second half is under way at Kenilworth Road!
Burnley start the second half on top as Koleosho evades the Luton defenders before driving the ball towards goal, but Kaminski makes a comfortable save.
Another chance for Burnley as Brownhill latches on to a throw inside the Luton box and powers a strike towards Kaminiski, who makes a smart stop to send the ball out for a corner.
CHANCE! Morris should do better.
The Luton striker does well to win a header inside the box from a corner but can only guide it over the bar.
Burnley are starting to knock on the door after a spell of pressure from Luton.
Luton are still yet to test Burnley's goal.
The Hatters have managed eight shots but have failed to hit the target so far.
The second half is end-to-end so far as Edwards' side look to get back into the game.
Burke brings down Koleosho and receives the second booking of the game.
Kabore leaves the pitch and is replaced by Adebayo as Edwards makes his second change of the game for Luton.
CHANCE! Luton almost equalise! Brown powers a header towards goal after an excellent delivery from Mpanzu, but Cullen clears off the line after the goalkeeper was beaten.
Roberts receives a yellow card for taking too long with a throw-in.
Morris goes down in the box under a challenge from Beyer, but the referee is having none of it.
Chong replaces Brown as Luton make their third and final change.
Luton have yet another chance from a corner but Morris once again can only power his header wide of Trafford's goal.
The Hatters are starting to apply the pressure at Kenilworth Road as Morris swivels and shoots inside the Burnley box, but Trafford gathers the ball comfortably.
Amdouni is replaced by Ramsey for Burnley.
Bruun Larsen enters the fray in place of Koleosho for Kompany's side.
Luton fail to take advantage from another corner as Adebayo heads wide of Trafford's right-hand post.
Edwards' men have had nine shots in the second half to Burnley's three as they continue to push for an equaliser.
Foster, who opened the scoring for Burnley, is replaced by Rodriguez.

GOOOOOAAAAL!!!!!!!! Luton equalise!!! 1-1! Chong sends a dangerous ball into the box which Burke nods down towards Adebayo, who holds off the defender and places the ball into the corner beyond Trafford!
Burke does superbly to climb above the Burnley defence and place a header into the path of Adebayo in the box.

GOAL!!!! 2-1 BURNLEY! Just a few seconds after the restart, the Clarets take the lead once again! Substitute Bruun Larsen unleashes a sensational strike from range to silence the Kenilworth Road faithful.
Assist Connor Richard John Roberts
Luton are pushing to try and equalise once again, but Burnley's goal has deflated Edwards' side.
The fourth official has indicated a minimum of seven minutes added time.
Chong is the latest player to go into the book late in the game.
Nakamba receives Luton's fourth booking of the game.
Ramsey is replaced by Delcroix as Burnley look to hold on.
Taylor receives a booking for kicking the ball away and delaying the restart.
Luton are filling the box as they look to equalise late on with a corner.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 BURNLEY
Burnley opened the scoring through Taylor just a few minutes before the half-time whistle, placing the ball beyond the goalkeeper after a superb throughball from Berge.
Late in the second half, Luton equalised through Adebayo, who came off the bench to finally get his side back in the game.
However, the Hatters' lead lasted just a few seconds, as Bruun Larsen unleashed a screamer from outside the box, which flew into the back of the net, earning the Clarets all three points.
Kompany's side secured their first win of the Premier League season and extended their unbeaten run to seven games against Luton.
The Clarets climb a place to 18th in the table as the Hatters remain in 17th on goal difference.
Edwards' men failed to build on their impressive win over Everton at the weekend, whilst Burnley bounced back from a disappointing defeat away at Newcastle United.
That's all for today, goodbye!
